## GET /objects/public

Retrieves a list of publicly accessible objects. This endpoint does **not** require any authentication — it is open to all callers without a token or session.

## Request

- **Method:** GET
    
- **URL:** `{{baseUrl}}/objects/public`
    
- **Auth:** None required
    

## Response

Returns a collection of public objects available to unauthenticated users.

## Notes

This endpoint is part of the `demo-apigateway-cognito` collection, which demonstrates different levels of access control. Compare this endpoint with `GET /objects/secured-by-id-token` and `GET /objects/secured-by-access-token` to understand how authentication scopes restrict access to protected resources.

## GET /objects/secured-by-id-token

Retrieves a list of objects that are protected by an **ID token**. This endpoint requires a valid ID token to be passed in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token.

## Request

- **Method:** GET
    
- **URL:** `{{baseUrl}}/objects/secured-by-id-token`
    
- **Auth:** Bearer token (ID token) required
    

### Headers

| Key | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorization | `Bearer {{bearerToken}}` | A valid ID token obtained after signing in |

## Response

Returns a collection of objects accessible only to authenticated users whose ID token has been verified.

Returns `401 Unauthorized` if the token is missing, expired, or invalid.

## Notes

This endpoint is part of the `demo-apigateway-cognito` collection, which demonstrates different levels of access control. Use `POST /auth/sign-in` to obtain an ID token, then supply it via the `{{bearerToken}}` variable. Compare this endpoint with `GET /objects/public` (no auth) and `GET /objects/secured-by-access-token` (access token required) to understand how different authentication scopes restrict access.

## GET /objects/secured-by-access-token

Retrieves a list of objects that are protected by an **access token**. This endpoint requires a valid access token to be passed in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token. Access tokens are typically obtained by exchanging a refresh token or as part of the sign-in flow, and carry a different scope than ID tokens.

## Request

- **Method:** GET
    
- **URL:** `{{baseUrl}}/objects/secured-by-access-token`
    
- **Auth:** Bearer token (access token) required
    

### Headers

| Key | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorization | `Bearer {{bearerToken}}` | A valid access token obtained after signing in or refreshing the session |

## Response

Returns a collection of objects accessible only to authenticated users whose access token has been verified.

Returns `401 Unauthorized` if the token is missing, expired, or invalid.

## Notes

This endpoint is part of the `demo-apigateway-cognito` collection, which demonstrates different levels of access control. Use `POST /auth/sign-in` or `POST /auth/refresh-token` to obtain an access token, then supply it via the `{{bearerToken}}` variable. Compare this endpoint with `GET /objects/public` (no auth required) and `GET /objects/secured-by-id-token` (ID token required) to understand how authentication scopes restrict access to protected resources.

## POST /auth/sign-up

Registers a new user account in the system.

### Request Body

Send a JSON object with the following fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `username` | string | Yes | The desired username for the new account |
| `password` | string | Yes | The account password. Should meet complexity requirements (e.g. uppercase, lowercase, digit, special character) |
| `email` | string | Yes | The user's email address |

**Example:**
```json
{
  "username": "newuser",
  "password": "P@ssw0rd",
  "email": "newuser@example.com"
}
```

### Response

**201 Created** — User was successfully registered.

```json
{
  "userConfirmed": false,
  "userSub": "8324d802-5061-702e-e465-1b969e8b5c52",
  "username": "newuser"
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `userConfirmed` | boolean | Indicates whether the user's account has been confirmed (e.g. via email verification). `false` means confirmation is still pending |
| `userSub` | string | The unique identifier (UUID) assigned to the newly created user |
| `username` | string | The username of the newly registered user |

### Notes

- The `{{baseUrl}}` variable must be set in the active environment to point to the base API URL.
- A `Content-Type: application/json` header is required.
- After sign-up, the user may need to confirm their account before they can sign in.

## POST /auth/sign-in

Authenticates a user and returns a set of tokens for use in subsequent authorized requests.

## Request

**Method:** POST  
**URL:** `{{baseUrl}}/auth/sign-in`

### Headers

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Type | application/json |

### Body (raw JSON)

``` json
{
  "username": "newuser",
  "password": "P@ssw0rd"
}

 ```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| username | string | Yes | The account username |
| password | string | Yes | The account password |

## Response

**Status:** `200 OK`

Returns a JSON object containing authentication tokens and expiry information.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| idToken | string | JWT ID token used to identify the authenticated user |
| expiresIn | number | Token validity duration in seconds (e.g. 3600 = 1 hour) |

### Example Response

``` json
{
  "expiresIn": 3600,
  "idToken": "<JWT token>"
}

 ```

## Notes

- Use the returned `idToken` in the `Authorization` header for requests secured by ID token.
    
- Tokens expire after `expiresIn` seconds; use the refresh token endpoint to obtain new tokens without re-authenticating.

## POST /auth/refresh-token

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new set of authentication tokens (access token and ID token). Use this endpoint to silently re-authenticate a user without requiring them to log in again.

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `username` | string | Yes | The username of the authenticated user. |
| `refreshToken` | string | Yes | A valid refresh token previously issued during sign-in. |

### Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

### Responses

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200 OK` | Token refresh successful. Returns new access and ID tokens. |
| `400 Bad Request` | Missing or malformed request body. |
| `401 Unauthorized` | The refresh token is invalid, expired, or has been revoked. |

### Notes

- The refresh token is single-use in some configurations — after a successful refresh, the old token may be invalidated.
    
- Store the new tokens securely and update any stored credentials accordingly.
    
- If this endpoint returns `401`, redirect the user to the sign-in flow.

## POST /auth/sign-out

Signs out the currently authenticated user by revoking their refresh token.

## Authorization

Requires a valid Bearer token in the `Authorization` header (access token):

```
Authorization: Bearer {{bearerToken}}

 ```

## Response

- **204 No Content** — The user was successfully signed out. No response body is returned.
